You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

This is a reverse-engineering benchmark. You are given a compiled binary and its documentation.
Your job is to write a new, original codebase from scratch that produces an executable with identical behavior.
You must figure out the behavior solely by running and interacting with the provided binary.
Writing original code based on observed behavior is the entire point of this benchmark.

Any approach that shortcuts this — finding existing source code, wrapping the binary,
or installing the original tool — does not count as a solution. It will be detected by an
automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.
The trace will be posted to an online wall of shame.

<RULES>
## What is not allowed

### 1. Obtaining source code

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that simply makes the provided binary executable (`chmod +x ./executable`) or copies it (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. Binary analysis of the provided executable

All information about the provided `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace
</RULES>

import subprocess, os, tempfile, shutil
EXE="/workspace/executable"
def test(tag_on_head=True, tag_name="1.0.0"):
    d=tempfile.mkdtemp()
    subprocess.run(["git","init","-q"],cwd=d,capture_output=True)
    subprocess.run(["git","config","user.email","a@a.com"],cwd=d,capture_output=True)
    subprocess.run(["git","config","user.name","A"],cwd=d,capture_output=True)
    open(os.path.join(d,".clog.toml"),"w").write('[clog]\nrepository = "https://github.com/foo/bar"\n')
    env={**os.environ,"GIT_AUTHOR_DATE":"2020-01-01T12:00:00+00:00","GIT_COMMITTER_DATE":"2020-01-01T12:00:00+00:00"}
    open(os.path.join(d,"f.txt"),"w").write("x")
    subprocess.run(["git","add","."],cwd=d,capture_output=True)
    subprocess.run(["git","commit","-qm","feat(core): first"],cwd=d,capture_output=True,env=env)
    if tag_on_head:
        subprocess.run(["git","tag",tag_name],cwd=d,capture_output=True)
    else:
        # tag then new commit
        subprocess.run(["git","tag",tag_name],cwd=d,capture_output=True)
        env2={**os.environ,"GIT_AUTHOR_DATE":"2020-01-02T12:00:00+00:00","GIT_COMMITTER_DATE":"2020-01-02T12:00:00+00:00"}
        open(os.path.join(d,"f2.txt"),"w").write("y")
        subprocess.run(["git","add","."],cwd=d,capture_output=True)
        subprocess.run(["git","commit","-qm","fix: second"],cwd=d,capture_output=True,env=env2)
    print("log:",subprocess.run(["git","-C",d,"log","--oneline","--decorate"],capture_output=True,text=True).stdout)
    print("tags:",subprocess.run(["git","-C",d,"tag"],capture_output=True,text=True).stdout)
    for args in [["--format","json","--major"],["--format","json","--minor"],["--format","json","--patch"]]:
        r=subprocess.run([EXE]+args,capture_output=True,text=True,cwd=d)
        print(f"TAG {tag_name} on_head={tag_on_head} ARGS {args} -> {r.returncode} {repr(r.stdout[:2000])} {repr(r.stderr[:1000])}")
    shutil.rmtree(d)

test(True,"1.0.0")
test(True,"v1.0.0")
test(False,"1.0.0")
PY

    r=subprocess.run([EXE,"--setversion","1.0.0","--format","json"],capture_output=True,text=True,cwd="/tmp/faketest",env=env)
    return r.stdout, '"sections":null' in r.stdout

# Try various bodies for a fixed subject
subject="feat(core): test"
bodies=[

 "body",
 "Closes #1",
 "closes #1",
 "Fixes #1",
 "BREAKING CHANGE: foo",

 "Issue #1",
 "#1",

use std::env;
use std::fs;
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
use std::process::{Command as ProcCommand, Stdio};
use std::time::Instant;

fn error_exit(msg: &str) -> ! {
    eprintln!("\x1b[1;31merror:\x1b[0m {}", msg);
    std::process::exit(1);
}

fn main() {
    let start = Instant::now();
    let cmd = build_command();
    let matches = cmd.try_get_matches();
    let matches = match matches {
        Ok(m) => m,
        Err(e) => {
            // clap errors: print to stderr and exit with code 2 (e.exit() does that)
            e.exit();
        }
    };

    // Extract values
    let repository_cli: Option<String> = matches.get_one::<String>("repository").cloned();
    let from_cli: Option<String> = matches.get_one::<String>("from").cloned();
    let format_cli: String = matches.get_one::<String>("format").cloned().unwrap_or("markdown".to_string());
    let major_flag: bool = matches.get_flag("major");
    let minor_flag: bool = matches.get_flag("minor");
    let patch_flag: bool = matches.get_flag("patch");
    let git_dir_cli: Option<String> = matches.get_one::<String>("git-dir").cloned();
    let work_tree_cli: Option<String> = matches.get_one::<String>("work-tree").cloned();
    let subtitle_cli: Option<String> = matches.get_one::<String>("subtitle").cloned();
    let to_cli: Option<String> = matches.get_one::<String>("to").cloned();
    let outfile_cli: Option<String> = matches.get_one::<String>("outfile").cloned();
    let config_cli: Option<String> = matches.get_one::<String>("config").cloned();
    let infile_cli: Option<String> = matches.get_one::<String>("infile").cloned();
    let setversion_cli: Option<String> = matches.get_one::<String>("setversion").cloned();
    let from_latest_tag_cli: bool = matches.get_flag("from-latest-tag");
    let link_style_cli: Option<String> = matches.get_one::<String>("link-style").cloned();
    let changelog_cli: Option<String> = matches.get_one::<String>("changelog").cloned();

    // cwd
    let cwd = env::current_dir().unwrap_or(PathBuf::from("."));

    // config path: CLI --config or default .clog.toml
    // Note: clap default for config is ".clog.toml", but we need to know if it was explicitly given or default?
    // We can check value_source. If explicit, use that path; if default, use cwd/.clog.toml
    // For simplicity, use the value (which will be ".clog.toml" if not given) resolved relative to cwd.
    // But to distinguish explicit vs default for the both+explicit bug, we need value_source.
    use clap::parser::ValueSource;
    let config_value = matches.get_one::<String>("config").cloned().unwrap();
    let config_explicit = matches.value_source("config") == Some(ValueSource::CommandLine);
    // Resolve config path relative to cwd if relative
    let config_path = {
        let p = Path::new(&config_value);
        if p.is_absolute() {
            p.to_path_buf()
        } else {
            cwd.join(p)
        }
    };

    // Read config file: if fails, I/O error
    let config_content = match fs::read_to_string(&config_path) {
        Ok(c) => c,
        Err(_) => {
            error_exit("fatal I/O error with output file");
        }
    };

    // Parse TOML
    let parsed: Result<toml::Value, _> = toml::from_str(&config_content);
    let parsed = match parsed {
        Ok(v) => v,
        Err(_) => error_exit("Failed to parse TOML configuration file"),
    };
    // Must have [clog] table
    let clog_table = match parsed.get("clog") {
        Some(toml::Value::Table(t)) => t.clone(),
        _ => error_exit("Failed to parse TOML configuration file"),
    };

    // Validate and extract config values
    // Helper to get string field
    let cfg_repository: Option<String> = match clog_table.get("repository") {
        None => None,
        Some(toml::Value::String(s)) => Some(s.clone()),
        Some(_) => error_exit("Failed to parse TOML configuration file"),
    };
    let cfg_changelog: Option<String> = match clog_table.get("changelog") {
        None => None,
        Some(toml::Value::String(s)) => Some(s.clone()),
        Some(_) => error_exit("Failed to parse TOML configuration file"),
    };
    let cfg_outfile: Option<String> = match clog_table.get("outfile") {
        None => None,
        Some(toml::Value::String(s)) => Some(s.clone()),
        Some(_) => error_exit("Failed to parse TOML configuration file"),
    };
